name: Apple Omelette
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Stew the apples, when you have pared and cored them, as for apple-sauce
Beat them very smooth while hot, adding the butter, sugar, and nutmeg
When perfectly cold, put with the eggs, which should be whipped light, yolks and whites separately
Put in the yolks first, then the rose-water, lastly the whites
Pour into a deep bake-dish, which has been warmed and buttered
Bake in a moderate oven until it is delicately browned
Eat warm—not hot—for tea, with Graham bread

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stew the apples, when you have pared and cored them, as for apple-sauce
2. Beat them very smooth while hot, adding the butter, sugar, and nutmeg
3. When perfectly cold, put with the eggs, which should be whipped light, yolks and whites separately
4. Put in the yolks first, then the rose-water, lastly the whites
5. Pour into a deep bake-dish, which has been warmed and buttered
6. Bake in a moderate oven until it is delicately browned
7. Eat warm—not hot—for tea, with Graham bread
